title: GROUP BY on events: hashed, sorted, mixed, spilled, and split into partial aggregates

steps.sql: SELECT id, kind FROM events WHERE id BETWEEN 20001 AND 20012 ORDER BY id
steps.note: twelve events and their kinds, in the order the table holds them.

steps.sql: SELECT kind, count(*) FROM events WHERE id BETWEEN 20001 AND 20012 GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind
steps.note: the same twelve, grouped by kind: the answer both strategies have to reach.

steps.sql:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT user_id, count(*) FROM events GROUP BY user_id
steps.note: events per user. nothing is sorted by user_id, so postgres hashes: one pass, one hash table entry per user.

data: ->  Seq Scan on events (actual rows=25000.00 loops=1)

steps.note: the same with hash aggregation switched off: sort all 25,000 rows by user_id first, then count each run of equal ids.

data: ->  Seq Scan on events (actual rows=25000.00 loops=1)

steps.note: ROLLUP: three groupings at once. two are hashed in one pass; the grand total needs no hashing at all.

data: ->  Seq Scan on events (actual rows=25000.00 loops=1)

steps.sql:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT user_id, count(*) FROM events GROUP BY user_id ORDER BY user_id
steps.note: with ORDER BY user_id on top: group first by hashing, then sort just the 500 groups.

data: ->  Seq Scan on events (actual rows=25000.00 loops=1)

steps.sql:
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT user_id, count(*), sum(amount) FROM events GROUP BY user_id
steps.note: the default 4MB: a sum and a count per user, all 500 groups in one hash table.

data: ->  Seq Scan on events (actual rows=25000.00 loops=1)

steps.note: 64kB: the hash table outgrows its budget. groups that don't fit are spilled to disk and finished in later batches.

data: Buffers: shared hit=335, temp read=22 written=45
->  Seq Scan on events (actual rows=25000.00 loops=1)

steps.note: with an index on user_id, the rows arrive sorted by user_id for free, and grouping just streams: a GroupAggregate with no Sort.

data: ->  Index Only Scan using events_user_id_idx on events (actual rows=25000.00 loops=1)
